Back in the day when I was a child in Australia, most cakes were “iced”. No one really knew any better back then, it was all recipes from Woman's Day magazine.

I think back to parties of my own, also friends parties – remembering sad looking little cupcakes with a thin layer of water/powered sugar mix on top, slightly oozing down the cupcake casing, like these.

They usually had some sprinkles added to the tops in an effort to make them look better. They look so under dressed for a nice party!

How things have changed since then, thankfully.

Most chain grocery stores DO NOT make their own frostings. They buy big 32lb tubs in bulk in various flavors and colors - mostly for vanilla it is white so the bakery staff can airbrush it. The list of ingredients in them makes me shudder!!

One thing I learnt in my Home Economics class in high school, that has always stuck with me. The first 3 things listed on an ingredients label are the 3 MAIN things in the product you are buying – something I always look at when shopping. The first 3 things on a huge tub of “fake frosting” are – Sugar, Shortening (various oils included in this) and water. The label close up.

Mmmmm doesn’t that sound yummy! I don’t know about you but it sounds extremely artificial and gross, not to mention that greasy feeling in your mouth you get from chain store cake. No one eats crisco out of a tub, so why would you want to slather it all over a cake?!?

Some smaller bakeries and home based bakers make their own frosting (buttercream) from scratch, using REAL butter. Yes it can be time consuming, there are many and varied ways to do it – ranging from simple steps to more complex.

Mine is icing sugar (powdered sugar) & butter as the base, now lets say a customer wanted strawberry buttercream right - I then go to the local farmers market to get fresh strawberries and I make my own strawberry reduction to add to the buttercream base. For vanilla, I get Madagascar vanilla bean paste and add that - tastes SOOO much better than vanilla essence from the store. I charge how I charge because I use good quality ingredients and don't take shortcuts.

People are all about food these days, how it’s made, what goes into it etc. If you are taking the time to get a cake, wouldn’t you want the ingredients to be as natural as possible?

Although I agree that store cake frosting isn't great, I think there is a place for shortening based frosting, they can be delicious. A Crisco based frosting can be incredibly creamy and it pipes nicely. Plus a vegetable shortening base is a great option if you are making something for a vegetarian.

I remember my grandma making frosting that was half butter and half shortening and it was the best frosting ever. I'm suspicious that grandma's shortening was not vegetable based but was probably just good old lard! Wish I had gotten the recipe from her before she passed. It was one of those unofficial ones that was never on paper. She'd just whip up a batch using "a little butter, a little shortening, some sugar, a few shakes of vanilla..."

Damn I miss grandma... :(

If I were to use something like that I would go the "Sweetex" route which is more expensive than store bought crisco and can be used in high ratio cake batters. It is better for hot climates as it holds better and won't just melt of a cake like traditional simple buttercream so it would be perfect for Florida or say Arizona.

As for vegetarians, it all depends on what side of the fence they are with eggs (being no fertilized most would eat) but I would only use egg whites in a swiss meringue buttercream but you would need to make sure that is covered under the cottage food section for home bakers seeing as it is something that can go bad in a hot environment potentially making people sick and for a store front bakery it would need to be sent out for testing before being able to sell to the public.

Sorry about your grandma :(
